story_text.value:
I originally made this addon 4 years ago, but recently discovered that coding agents love it.

The addon adds a scripting API for Blender’s node trees, such as Geometry Nodes or Shader Nodes.

It generates a function and related types for every node in Blender. Then the agent (or you) can write scripts to create node trees without having to guess what the node, input, and output names are.

It’s meant to be used alongside the Blender MCP.

In my tests, Opus finishes building node trees in at least half the time using at least half the tokens to answer the same prompt.

Because the scripting API forces it to build correct node trees, it has to back track less to fix mistakes. This saves a lot of time and tokens. There is also a skill and some helper functions to let it look up the function signatures for nodes.

Let me know how it works for you!

title.value: Show HN: A Blender addon that makes Claude twice as efficient at using nodes

story_text.value:
I created this webpage to compare the rates for trash hauling across the San Francisco Bay Area.

I wanted to see how Oakland California compares to the rest of the region. I knew the rates were high, but I wanted to quantify how high. Especially since the cost of proper trash disposal contributes substantially to Oakland's illegal dumping problem.

I found some interesting insights between wealthiest cities on the peninsula and Oakland, because a city like Atherton actually pays substantially less than Oakland for 20 gallon trash service. I would have expected the operational expenditure related to service delivery to be lower in Oakland, so rates would be lower.

Also, trash hauling has some well-publicized cases of corruption (including the current federal indictment aginst former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao involving waste collection executives).

I think the transparency provided by a webpage like this can only be a good thing.

Please let me know what you think and any feedback.

story_text.value:
Hey HN!

I shared Optio here back in March. Originally it was focused on getting swarms of coding agents (claude code/codex) to drive PRs towards a merge by automatically resuming them on CI failures or PR comments.

Since then, I've reworked the project to be a general platform for running any kind of AI workflow on your infra by allowing users to configure each component of a possible workflow:

When: On demand, a cron schedule, or triggered by external events such as a webhook, slack message, ticket (jira/linear/gh), pagerduty/datadog/alertsmanager/pylon/sentry.

Where: In a k8s pod or any machine you have installed the optio daemon on (I use my laptop).

Who: Any harness you prefer (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Pi, etc.)

What/Why: You can format parameters from the triggers directly into the prompts and then configure if the agent should exit, be resumed automatically, or be persistent.

You can either define workflows in the web ui or as yaml files that get synced to the orchestrator (ai config-as-code).

I've also built native iOS and Android apps so you can connect to your cluster and create/manage agents remotely.

The marketing page is at https://optio.host and the code is still open source at https://github.com/jonwiggins/optio

Would love feedback or any thoughts you might have on how I could make it better!

story_text.value:
Hey HN! As an avid user of cmux (https://cmux.com/), I wanted a way to control terminal and agent sessions from my Android phone, so I built Muxer. The app talks to a tiny relay over HTTPS, that then talks to cmux through its local socket, and gives you to ability to:

  - Answer agent permission requests, questions and plans from a notification
  - Reply to Claude Code, Codex and Pi chat sessions with text, voice, @ file mentions and photos
  - Receive all cmux notification, with inline replies, bubbles and background delivery.
  - Use a live terminal with sticky modifier keys and local scrollback
  - Share text and links from any app to an agent
  - Organize workspaces
  - Manage cmux Cloud VMs and automations
  - Lock the app with your fingerprint, face or screen lock
Enjoy, and let me know what you think!

story_text.value:
This is my own very opinionated take on personal accounting / budgeting for freelancers and small business owners operating in multiple currencies.

A lot of this is influenced by my circumstances:

- consultant / freelancer / business owner with multiple revenue streams - revenue fluctuates a lot and changes month to month - we're nomad, so currencies and shops change a lot, but categories stay stable - mobile and agentic first (PWA and MCP) with good desktop support on top - import from Wise, Plaid (so most banks), CSV, + screenshots and PDFs from mobile apps when all else fails - automatic categorization that does the right thing 90% of the time and learns for your corrections - deployed on a CloudFlare account (free account is usually enough)

Think of this as a template - just hand the repo URL to your agent and go wild. This is built to be infinitely malleable and extendable because accounting setups and needs differ so much between people.

Extracted from my own heavily used setup after removing all the private and unique bits.

May we all take control of our funds, each in our unique way.
